clue.text: Faith and Richard catching cheat at last, Mark a victim of this?

parts.note: faith in someone is trust or assurance

indicators.note: what comes at last is the final item, so only the closing letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of cheat
Rick is a short form of Richard

explanation.surface: Two people, Faith and Richard, finally catch out a cheat, and someone called Mark seems to have been the dupe.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a man's name, but a mark is the target of a swindler. Richard catches the T by having it placed just before him.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle that wins a dupe's trust before cheating him is a con; its victim is called the mark.

clue.text: Saddle king's horse

parts.note: to saddle someone with a duty is to charge them with it
R is short for rex, Latin for king; the 's is read as 'has'

explanation.surface: An instruction to put the saddle on the king's horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Saddle looks like the leather seat but works as a verb meaning to burden someone with a task.
explanation.definitionFit: A charger is a war horse ridden by a knight or cavalry officer into battle.

clue.text: Chip and PIN ultimately a chore on leaving

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so those letters are taken out of the word
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of PIN
taken as written
a household task
re means on or about, as in a letter heading; these letters go

explanation.surface: Chip and PIN, the card-payment system, turns out to be a chore in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Chip and PIN is a familiar phrase for paying by card, but chip is the definition on its own. RE for 'on' (concerning) is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, usually served loaded with melted cheese and salsa as a snack.

clue.text: One lair, with fox cub climbing on it, is uninteresting

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
an animal's home

indicators.note: in a down answer, climbing goes upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a young fox is a kit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fox's den with a cub scrambling over it is described as dull.
explanation.walkthrough: A young fox is a kit, a less familiar word than cub; 'with' and 'on' just place the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Identikit, from the police face-building kit, describes something formulaic and typical, lacking any individual character.

clue.text: Rising astronomy teacher covers the beginning of a term

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means going upwards, so read the letters from the bottom
what covers something keeps it inside, so the letters sit within the words

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming astronomy teacher covers how a term begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a school term starting, but term here is a word.
explanation.definitionFit: An etymon is the earlier root form from which a word is derived, so it is where a word originates.

clue.text: Seducer caught when American banker turned up

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
A is a standard abbreviation for American

indicators.note: turned up in a down answer means flipped upwards, so the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: a banker in crosswords is a river, something with banks; the Avon is an English river

explanation.surface: A seducer was caught out when an American banker appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: Banker looks like a financier but is a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Casanova was a famous Venetian lover, and his name is used for any womaniser.

clue.text: Spare can husband fills

indicators.note: what fills something goes inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a tin is a can
the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband fills up a spare can.
explanation.walkthrough: Spare reads as extra, but here it is the adjective meaning lean.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare figure is lean and slim, without any surplus flesh.

clue.text: Ignorant, eat and drink carelessly around hospital

indicators.note: to go around something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another
doing something carelessly leaves it in disorder, so the letters get jumbled

parts.note: the two verbs taken as written
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Someone clueless eats and drinks messily while at a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters of the two verbs are arranged around the H.
explanation.definitionFit: To be kept in the dark is to be uninformed, an idiom for not knowing what is going on.

clue.text: Knocking out illicit gin okay?

indicators.note: illicit means unlawful or bent, so the letters are crooked out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether bootleg gin, which can knock you out, is all right.
explanation.walkthrough: KO is boxing shorthand for knockout, and kayo is its spelt-out form, usable as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To kayo a boxer is to deliver a KO, flooring him so he cannot rise in time.

clue.text: Vault tracks with European in pursuit

indicators.note: to be in something is to be inside it, so one piece is placed within the rest

parts.note: a vault is an arched roof
E is the abbreviation for European
RY is the abbreviation for railway, which runs on tracks

explanation.surface: A pole vaulter clears the bar and runs down the track with a European chasing him.
explanation.walkthrough: In pursuit looks like a single phrase meaning chasing; split it, and pursuit becomes the definition, a hobby or sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting with bow and arrow is a sport or pastime, which is one sense of a pursuit.

clue.text: E.g. entertaining at home, extremely thoughtful? Good

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests has them inside, so one piece holds others

parts.note: say, like e.g., introduces an example
someone at home is in

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of thoughtful

explanation.surface: Hosting guests at home, for example, is a thoughtful and good thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: E.g. and say are interchangeable ways of offering an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintly describes someone very virtuous, holy or morally upright, which is what good means here.

clue.text: Neglected patch in Spooner's brown robe

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds trade places

parts.note: to toast bread is to brown it
a gown is a long robe
swap the opening sounds of the two words just found

explanation.surface: A worn spot on a brown dressing gown.
explanation.walkthrough: Toast gown, with its opening sounds swapped, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserted town, abandoned by its inhabitants, is a neglected place where nobody lives any more.

clue.text: Short clue faced by you once: "Beast from the East?"

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: ye is the old form of you
a tip is a hint or clue; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A brief clue offered to you, the solver, long ago about the Beast from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beast from the East was the 2018 cold snap in Britain; here it is a creature from Asia. 'Faced by' puts YE in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman is said to roam the Himalayas, an eastern beast of legend.

clue.text: Produce another cake without topping, a reason for moving mince pies to one side

indicators.note: without its top, a word loses its first letter

parts.words: a reason for moving mince pies to one side
parts.note: REM, rapid eye movement, makes the eyes dart about in sleep; mince pies is rhyming slang for eyes
taken as written; its first letter goes

explanation.surface: A baker makes another cake without icing, having pushed the mince pies aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Mince pies is Cockney rhyming slang for eyes, so the long phrase is REM, the rapid eye movement of dreaming sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To remake something is to make it again, creating a second version of an earlier work.

clue.text: Two shakes new French chef bringing in time for summit

indicators.note: bringing something in introduces it among the rest, so one piece is set inside

parts.note: in two shakes means in a moment, and a mo is a moment
the standard abbreviation for new
the abbreviation for time
Raymond Blanc is a French chef famous in Britain

explanation.surface: In no time a new French chef is brought in for a top-level meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Summit suggests a conference, but it is a mountain top. Two shakes, as in 'in two shakes', is a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest mountain in the Alps rises on the French-Italian border, so it is a peak.

clue.text: Beetle on drape

parts.note: on top of is over
to drape cloth is to hang it

explanation.surface: An insect sitting on a curtain.
explanation.walkthrough: Beetle is a verb here, as in beetling brows or cliffs that jut out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that beetles projects outward over what is below, as a cliff edge juts out.

clue.text: Again lights sway — it's the start of engineers' drills

parts.note: to hold sway is to rule or reign

indicators.note: a drill bores into something, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of engineers

explanation.surface: The lights swing about again as the engineers start drilling.
explanation.walkthrough: Drills looks like a noun, as in training exercises, but it is the verb: the E bores into IT'S.
explanation.definitionFit: To reignite a fire or lamp is to set it alight once more, starting a flame anew.

clue.text: When struggling, I drop price, putting out advertising once in a while

indicators.note: something struggling is thrashing about, so the letters are thrown into disorder
putting something out ejects it, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
PR, public relations, is publicity work; these letters go

explanation.surface: A struggling shop cuts its prices and drops its advertising now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove a P and an R from the ten letters and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Periodic describes things recurring at intervals, so they happen from time to time rather than constantly.

clue.text: Feature of Christmas from Long Island I will miss

parts.note: to long for something is to pine for it

indicators.note: what you miss is absent, so that letter goes missing from the word

parts.note: Tiree is an island of the Inner Hebrides, off western Scotland
taken as written; this is the letter removed

explanation.surface: Someone will miss a Christmas custom from Long Island, New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Long Island looks like one place but splits into a verb and an island. TIREE is a small Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: A fir or other conifer is commonly decorated indoors as the centrepiece of seasonal festivities.

clue.text: Perhaps three at St Andrews rendezvous snubbed upstart

indicators.note: a snub nose is short, so snubbing clips the word's end

parts.note: St Andrews is a famous golf course in Scotland, and a hole may be a par three
a meeting place; its final letter goes

explanation.surface: At a golf meeting in St Andrews, a social climber was snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: Three at a golf course suggests a score, and par is the standard score for a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is a person of humble origins who has newly risen to wealth and is resented for it.

clue.text: Sports presenter losing heart, becoming continuity announcer?

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, and losing it removes the central letter

parts.note: Gary Lineker, ex-England striker, long presented BBC's Match of the Day

explanation.surface: A sports broadcaster, losing his passion, ends up introducing programmes between shows.
explanation.walkthrough: Gary Lineker is a British football presenter. The question mark flags a definition by description.
explanation.definitionFit: A continuity announcer joins one programme to the next, so he connects or bridges between items.

clue.text: Lyricists working with ABBA?

parts.note: surface reading: songwriters collaborating with the Swedish pop group
setter's reading: ABBA is a rhyme scheme, lines one and four sharing one sound, two and three another

explanation.walkthrough: The pop group is a red herring; ABBA is the notation poets use for an enclosed rhyme scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of verse who match line endings by sound follow patterns labelled with letters like ABBA.

clue.text: Commotion round drunk

parts.note: to raise a stink is to cause a commotion
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Round reads as a round of drinks but simply gives the letter shaped like a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinko is a slang adjective for heavily intoxicated, meaning very much the worse for alcohol.

clue.text: Guys in Costa finish off coffees

parts.note: costa is the Latin and anatomical word for a rib

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of coffees

explanation.surface: Some men in a Costa coffee shop finish their drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Costa looks like the British coffee chain but is the Latin word for rib. Guys is a verb, as in making fun of.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to tease or mock them, the same as ribbing them good-humouredly.

clue.text: Very hip, playing Steely Dan's latest cuts

parts.note: what is hip is fashionable, or in

indicators.note: playing with something moves it around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the latest thing comes last, so only the final letter of the name is kept

parts.note: the last letter of Dan

explanation.surface: Playing Steely Dan's newest tracks is very cool.
explanation.walkthrough: Steely Dan is a US rock band and cuts are album tracks; the surface hangs together, but the cuts add no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Very and intensely are both intensifying adverbs, meaning to a high or extreme degree.

clue.text: Remove earwax, occasionally syringe emptied

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, so only its outside letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Instructions for clearing earwax: now and then, empty a syringe into the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove reads as a medical instruction about the wax, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase something is to wipe it out or delete it, removing all trace of it.

clue.text: College closed between terms for police investigation

indicators.note: something between two others is flanked by them, so it goes in the middle
a term is an end or limit, so only the final letters of the words are taken

parts.note: the last letter of police
a door pulled to is closed
the last letter of investigation

explanation.surface: A college shut down between terms so police could investigate.
explanation.walkthrough: Terms looks like school terms but means the ends of the last two words. To meaning closed is as in 'push the door to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is the famous English public school near Windsor, founded by Henry VI.

clue.text: Old routine news chief demanded and received

parts.note: ex means former
a performer's routine is an act
ED is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A former editor insisted on his usual routine and got it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a two-part phrase: insisting on something and then obtaining it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact a payment or concession is to insist on it and obtain it, often forcefully.

clue.text: Eccentric character in Greece a sect converts

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: to convert something is to change its form, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An oddball in Greece wins followers to a religious sect.
explanation.walkthrough: Character in the surface means a person, but it is a letter of an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutcase is an informal word for a crazy or very strange person, an oddball.

clue.text: Universal consensus is wrong about prisoner being out

parts.note: U is the film classification for universal

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece encloses another
something wrong is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a con is a convict

explanation.surface: The general agreement that a prisoner is being released is mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: Being out reads as being released from jail, but it means being knocked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone out cold has lost awareness, the state of not being conscious, as after a knockout.
